name: Bergen Pediatric Dentistry
healthgradesEvidence: Strongest Healthgrades signal in the closest group: 6 ratings, all five-star, with 3 written reviews.
healthgradesNegativeSummary: No negative rating, written complaint, or improvement tag appeared in the six Healthgrades ratings. The sample is still small.
acceptsNewPatients: Yes — Healthgrades and the practice site both indicate new patients are accepted; confirm by phone.
trainingSummary: Columbia University College of Dental Medicine; more than 30 years in practice; pediatric specialty training and behavior-focused care.
schoolContext: Columbia is an established university-based dental school with advanced specialty training and academic medical-center exposure. Dental schools do not have a single authoritative national ranking, so this is treated as a training-strength signal, not a score.
certificationsAwards: Practice site reports American Board of Pediatric Dentistry certification, Board Certified Behavior Analyst status, national health-and-wellness coaching certification, Columbia recognition for special-needs dentistry, and the Francis Black Humanitarian Award.
longTermFit: Excellent fit from age two through adolescence. The pediatric specialty, prevention focus, behavior-analysis training, airway/growth interest, and special-needs experience support continuity as a child matures.
secondaryReviewSummary: Google remains very strong. One older Yelp complaint lacked enough detail to establish a clinical pattern, and the theme was not repeated on Healthgrades.

name: Say Cheez Pediatric Dentistry & Orthodontics
healthgradesEvidence: Both Healthgrades ratings are five-star and both include written reviews, but the sample is very small.
healthgradesNegativeSummary: No negative rating or written complaint appeared on Healthgrades. With only two reviews, absence of criticism is not strong proof by itself.
acceptsNewPatients: Yes — the practice explicitly welcomes new patients; verify current insurance and availability.
trainingSummary: UCLA School of Dentistry; pediatric residency at Mount Sinai Medical Center; served as chief resident.
schoolContext: UCLA is a major research dental school and Mount Sinai provides academic medical-center specialty training. This is a strong training pathway, not a guarantee of chairside fit.
certificationsAwards: Board-certified pediatric dentist. The practice reports selection to Incisal Edge's 40 Under 40 class of 2026; that is an industry recognition, not a clinical board credential.
longTermFit: Excellent normal-development fit from first teeth through the early twenties, with pediatric care and in-house orthodontics that can reduce transitions later.
secondaryReviewSummary: Google volume is high and overwhelmingly positive, with no repeated negative clinical or administrative theme found.

name: Pediatric Dental Associates
healthgradesEvidence: Healthgrades shows four five-star ratings but no written review text or tags to audit.
healthgradesNegativeSummary: No low Healthgrades rating is present, but there is no written review text to analyze. This is a favorable but thin signal.
negativeClassification: No negative rating; no written detail
acceptsNewPatients: Yes — Healthgrades lists Dr. Zimmer as accepting new patients; confirm scheduling by phone.
trainingSummary: University of Pennsylvania School of Dental Medicine; Children's Hospital of Philadelphia fellowship; pediatric residency at Cincinnati Children's/Nationwide Children's; long-time Hackensack University Medical Center faculty affiliation.
schoolContext: Penn and the named children's hospitals are established academic training centers. The pediatric hospital pathway is especially relevant to treating children, though it does not replace direct review evidence.
certificationsAwards: AAPD member and long-standing hospital dental-faculty service are documented. I did not find a current board-certification claim on Healthgrades, so call the office if ABPD status matters to you.
longTermFit: Excellent continuity option for a typical two-year-old through adolescence, with behavior management, special-needs care, orthodontics, and a long-established multi-specialist practice.
secondaryReviewSummary: The much larger Google-derived review set is strongly positive, including gentle care and calming fearful children; no repeated safety concern surfaced.

name: Glen Rock Smiles Pediatric Dentistry & Orthodontics
healthgradesEvidence: One five-star Healthgrades rating says he has a great way with children; one review is too little to establish a pattern.
healthgradesNegativeSummary: No negative Healthgrades rating or tag appears, but the single-review sample is a major limitation.
acceptsNewPatients: Yes — the practice invites new pediatric appointments; confirm directly.
trainingSummary: University of Missouri–Kansas City DDS; University of Michigan Hospital general residency; Nova Southeastern pediatric specialty training.
schoolContext: The combination includes an academic hospital residency plus a dedicated pediatric specialty program. All are recognized professional training settings; no single dental-school ranking is used.
certificationsAwards: American Board of Pediatric Dentistry certified. The practice reports a 2019 New Jersey 'Favorite Kids' Doc' recognition; this is a parent/market recognition rather than board certification.
longTermFit: Very good from ages zero to two through the teen years. Pediatric dentistry and orthodontics are in the same practice, supporting long-term continuity.
secondaryReviewSummary: Google and Yelp-indexed material is strongly positive without a repeated complaint pattern, but total volume is smaller than Tier 1.

name: Dentistry for Children of Lodi
healthgradesEvidence: The largest useful Healthgrades sample here: 17 ratings, 82% five-star and 12% one-star; four written reviews are available.
healthgradesNegativeSummary: The visible critical written review praises Dr. Stillman but criticizes a different, newly hired dentist's experience and bedside manner. That is a credible provider-assignment concern, not evidence of unsafe care by Dr. Stillman. Anonymous one-star ratings remain unexplained.
negativeClassification: Serious enough to request a named provider
acceptsNewPatients: Yes — online booking is available; request Dr. Stillman specifically if choosing this practice.
trainingSummary: NYU College of Dentistry; NYU post-graduate pediatric residency; Healthgrades also lists earlier Moscow dental training.
schoolContext: NYU is a large, established dental school with substantial specialty training. The completed pediatric residency is more relevant here than any generalized school prestige claim.
certificationsAwards: Pediatric specialty training is documented. Confirm current ABPD certification directly; Healthgrades does not clearly name the certifying board on this profile.
longTermFit: Good long-term fit when booked with the experienced pediatric specialist. A recent Healthgrades review specifically describes care beginning at age two or three and continuing successfully.
secondaryReviewSummary: Google and community reviews repeat front-desk disorganization, rude interactions, and long waits. These operational complaints are credible, not merely impatient families, but do not form a recurring clinical-safety pattern.

name: SmileKidz Pediatric Dentistry & Braces
healthgradesEvidence: Healthgrades shows one five-star rating and no written review. It also labels the specialty only as dentistry, so the official board credential needs to carry more weight than the profile taxonomy.
healthgradesNegativeSummary: No negative Healthgrades rating appears, but there is no written text to audit and only one rating.
acceptsNewPatients: Yes — a current new-patient package is offered; confirm insurance.
trainingSummary: Rutgers School of Dental Medicine DMD; Montefiore general residency; University of Florida pediatric specialty training.
schoolContext: Rutgers is New Jersey's public dental school, and the later University of Florida specialty program is the key pediatric credential. The multi-stage pathway is relevant to long-term child care.
certificationsAwards: Official practice biography states American Board of Pediatric Dentistry certification. Healthgrades does not display that credential clearly, so it should be verified when booking.
longTermFit: Very good for routine care from toddler years onward, with pediatric prevention and orthodontic services available in the practice.
secondaryReviewSummary: Google's large review set is overwhelmingly positive; the lone low score did not reveal a corroborated clinical pattern.

name: Dental Care 4 Kids
healthgradesEvidence: Healthgrades shows 13 ratings: 69% five-star, 8% four-star, and 23% one-star. Only one written review is visible, and it is positive.
healthgradesNegativeSummary: Three of thirteen ratings are one-star, but Healthgrades provides no written explanation for them. That is a real caution signal, but it cannot responsibly be labeled impatience, billing, or clinical harm without text.
acceptsNewPatients: Yes — new-patient forms are available; verify insurance and desired provider.
trainingSummary: University of Maryland School of Dentistry; Monmouth Medical Center general residency; Lutheran Medical Center pediatric residency, serving as chief resident.
schoolContext: Maryland is the world's first dental college and an established academic dental school. The chief pediatric residency role is the most directly relevant training signal.
certificationsAwards: Official biography states American Board of Pediatric Dentistry certification. No distinct clinical award was relied on for tiering.
longTermFit: Strong clinical fit for infants through adolescence, including preventive coaching and special healthcare needs; the long drive and unexplained low Healthgrades ratings are the tradeoffs.
secondaryReviewSummary: Google and Yelp are much more favorable. A small billing discrepancy was reportedly resolved promptly; no repeated clinical-safety theme was found.

name: Riverfront Pediatric Dentistry
healthgradesEvidence: The office page has no reviews. Dr. Simchi's profile has two ratings split between five-star and one-star; only the five-star rating has written text.
healthgradesNegativeSummary: The one-star Healthgrades rating has no written explanation or tags. It is a genuine conflict signal, but there is no evidence to classify it as unreasonable impatience or a serious clinical event.
acceptsNewPatients: Yes — Healthgrades says Dr. Simchi accepts new patients; online scheduling is available.
trainingSummary: UMDNJ–New Jersey Dental School; two-year pediatric residency at Maimonides Medical Center; Healthgrades lists board certification in 2014.
schoolContext: The UMDNJ program is now Rutgers School of Dental Medicine, New Jersey's public dental school. Maimonides adds dedicated hospital-based pediatric specialty training.
certificationsAwards: Official biography states board certification, Dean's List, the American Academy of Esthetic Dentistry Award of Merit, and dental honor-society selection. The awards are academic/professional signals, not substitutes for review evidence.
longTermFit: Clinically well designed for toddlers through adolescence, with unusually strong child-engagement evidence. It is placed lower only because Healthgrades is now primary and its tiny rating set is sharply split.
secondaryReviewSummary: Google and Yelp are overwhelmingly favorable with no repeated clinical or administrative complaint, which conflicts with the sparse Healthgrades rating split.

name: Ridgewood Valley Pediatric Dentistry
healthgradesEvidence: The practice now identifies Dr. Nick Avianto as its dentist, but I could not locate a matching Healthgrades profile. Older Healthgrades reviews for a prior dentist were not carried forward.
healthgradesNegativeSummary: There is no current-provider Healthgrades review set to assess. This is an evidence gap, not a negative finding.
acceptsNewPatients: The official site invites new patients; confirm that Dr. Avianto is the treating provider and ask about current availability.
trainingSummary: The official site confirms pediatric practice focus but did not expose enough verifiable education detail in the reviewed page to score school or residency strength.
schoolContext: Not scored because a current Healthgrades education record and a detailed official training biography were not found. Ask for dental school, pediatric residency, and ABPD status.
certificationsAwards: No certification or award was used for tiering because current credentials could not be independently matched to Healthgrades.
longTermFit: The practice model is appropriate for children, but long-term confidence depends on confirming the current dentist's pediatric specialty training and board status before booking.
secondaryReviewSummary: Google and other secondary material are strongly positive, including toddler visits, but those reviews cannot replace current provider-level Healthgrades and credential verification.

name: Pediatric Dentistry of Teaneck
healthgradesEvidence: Dr. Shon's Healthgrades profile has two ratings split between five-star and one-star, with no written reviews or tags.
healthgradesNegativeSummary: The one-star Healthgrades rating is unexplained. It cannot be categorized as patient impatience, administration, or clinical harm without text.
acceptsNewPatients: Yes — both Healthgrades and the practice site indicate new patients are accepted; request Dr. Shon by name.
trainingSummary: University of North Carolina School of Dentistry; pediatric specialty training at Maimonides Medical Center; served as chief resident.
schoolContext: UNC is an established public dental school and Maimonides provides hospital-based pediatric specialty training. The residency and chief role are the most relevant signals.
certificationsAwards: Official biography states Dr. Shon is a diplomate of the American Board of Pediatric Dentistry. No separate award was relied on.
longTermFit: The named provider is well trained for infants through adolescence, but the practice's repeated administrative complaints and thin, split Healthgrades record reduce confidence for a long-term dental home.
secondaryReviewSummary: Multiple Google and Facebook reviews describe billing, insurance, phone, cancellation, and reception problems. One complaint involved family lateness, but the broader administrative pattern is too consistent to dismiss as impatience. No equally clear safety pattern was found.
